title: Court booking schema in PostgreSQL
idea: The schema stores each booked court hour as its own row, so one partial unique index makes PostgreSQL refuse any second live booking for that hour.

analogy.text: A pigeonhole rack, one hole per court and hour. A live booking puts a card in its holes; a filled hole takes no second card.
analogy.breaks: Cancelled cards stay in the rack, just marked inactive.

points: `booking` holds the money, status and deadline; `booking_slot` holds one row per hour.
The unique index covers only active rows, so cancelled hours can be rebooked.
CHECK constraints guard status values, time order and the PENDING deadline.
The reserve transaction expires stale holds first, then inserts every hour.

hero.title: The index that prevents double booking

parts.label: unique
parts.note: Two rows with the same key cannot both exist. A second insert fails with code 23505.

parts.label: name
parts.note: The name comes back in the error, so the API can map it to SLOT_TAKEN.

parts.label: table
parts.note: One row per booked court hour, not per booking. A two-hour booking adds two rows.

parts.label: key
parts.note: The pair that must be unique: this court at this hour. It also serves the grid query.

parts.label: partial
parts.note: Only live rows count. Cancelling or expiring sets active to false and frees the hour.

code.title: Tables and constraints
code.caption: The schema on a real PostgreSQL 18, five writes it refuses by itself, and the availability grid for one evening.

walk.text: Fixed venue data. Sport is TEXT with a named CHECK instead of a database enum.
`booking`: BIGINT money, a status CHECK, a unique Idempotency-Key, and two named rules.
One index serves 'my bookings'; a partial one lets the hold-expiry job find due holds.
`booking_slot` rows plus the partial unique index: the core invariant lives here.
Each bad write prints the Postgres error code and the constraint that stopped it.
Cancel BK-1 in one query string, which runs as one transaction. Now 19:00 is free for BK-2.
The grid query: a series of hours left-joined to live slot rows.

code.title: The reserve transaction
code.caption: Two parallel requests share 19:00 and exactly one wins; then an expired hold is taken over. A trimmed schema keeps the demo short.

walk.text: One client from the pool, one transaction per reserve call.
Expire this court's overdue holds and free their hours, in the same transaction.
Insert the booking as PENDING with a ten-minute deadline.
Insert one row per hour. A clash waits for the other transaction, then fails with 23505.
Two clients race for overlapping hours. Print how many won, never who; the winner pays.
BK-C's hold expires, BK-D takes 07:00, and BK-C's late confirm changes no rows.
Final counts prove the rules: one race winner, one expiry, three live hours.

pitfalls: Use c12's range exclusion for free-form times; whole-hour slots need only a unique key.
Do not check availability with SELECT and then insert; let the index decide.
Store times as TIMESTAMPTZ and convert to the ground's zone only for display.

quiz.q: What is the first line reserve.mjs prints?
options: It changes from run to run
quiz.why: Both inserts need the 19:00 row. The second waits for the first transaction, then the partial unique index rejects it with 23505.

takeaway: One row per court hour plus a partial unique index stops double booking.
